items.title: Mod Exceptions report shows a stale list after navigating back, and needs a View on Nexus link
items.why: Director confirmed live: adding a mod from Rebuild Missing Files, then going to the Mod Exceptions report, shows the OLD list until a full page reload -- the report only fetches once per page session. Also wants a direct link to the mod's Nexus page per row.
items.prompt:
TWO REAL ISSUES on the Mod Exceptions report, director's own live testing (2026-08-15).

1. STALE LIST AFTER NAVIGATING BACK: added "1DustAdeptArmorSE" via Rebuild Missing Files' own 'Add to Exception List' row button, then went to Reports > Mod Exceptions -- the new entry did NOT show under 'Currently excepted' (an unrelated stray 'Added "1DustAdeptArmorSE".' message was visible near the Add form instead -- investigate what's actually producing that text live, don't assume its source). A full page reload (not just re-navigating the sub-tab) then showed the entry correctly.
   ROOT CAUSE, confirmed via code read: `web/public/mod-exceptions-report-app.js`'s `loadModExceptionsReportPageOnce()` only ever fetches once per page load (`if (mePageLoaded) return;`) -- if this Reports sub-tab was already visited earlier in the same browser session (loading whatever the list looked like at that moment), navigating back to it later never re-fetches, so it silently shows stale data instead of the real current list. A full page reload is the only thing that resets `mePageLoaded` to `false`.
   FIX: the report needs to actually reflect the current list every time it's opened, not just the first time in a page session. Simplest correct fix: drop the once-only guard and re-fetch (`meLoad()`) every time this sub-tab becomes visible -- check how sibling reports handle this (e.g. does Workshop Report re-fetch on every visit, or does it have its own deliberate caching reason that's different here). If a real caching reason exists elsewhere in this codebase for the once-only pattern, don't just delete it blind -- confirm this report doesn't have the same reason before changing it.
   Also investigate the stray 'Added "1DustAdeptArmorSE".' text live -- is it genuinely a leftover DOM state from an earlier real add-form use in the same session, or something else? Don't guess; check what actually produces that text and why it was visible in this scenario.

2. ADD A LINK TO VIEW THE MOD ON NEXUS (director's own request): each row already stores an optional Nexus mod id. Add a 'View on Nexus' link/button per row (only shown when `modId` is present, same conditional pattern Workshop Report already uses for its own View on Nexus action) -- the real URL format is `https://www.nexusmods.com/skyrimspecialedition/mods/<modId>` (reuse this project's own existing Nexus-URL-building helper if one already exists for mod pages specifically, rather than hardcoding the URL string fresh -- check `web/public/app.js`/`nexusCollectionUrl`-style helpers first for a mod-page equivalent; if none exists, this is a small enough URL to build inline, but check first).

VERIFY LIVE: reproduce the exact stale-list repro (add from Rebuild Missing Files, navigate to the report WITHOUT a full reload, confirm the entry now shows immediately) and confirm the Nexus link renders correctly and opens the real mod page for an entry that has a modId, and correctly doesn't show one for an entry that doesn't. Handoff with what you tested.

items.title: Rebuild Missing Files: 'Try Again' on the Vortex-running modal does nothing
items.why: Director confirmed live: after closing Vortex and clicking Try Again, no scan starts -- the retry callback is hardcoded to an empty no-op function across every error site on this page, not just the one that failed. Currently the only recovery is going back to the collection picker and starting over.
items.prompt:
REAL BUG, director-confirmed live: on Rebuild Missing Files, picking collections and moving to the scan step while Vortex is still open correctly shows the 'Vortex is running' modal -- but after closing Vortex and clicking that modal's own **Try Again** button, nothing happens. No scan starts. The only way to recover is going all the way back to the collection picker and starting over.

ROOT CAUSE, confirmed via code read, exact line: `web/public/rebuild-missing-app.js`'s shared `rmfHandleError(e, box)` (~line 34-37) hits its `vortex-running` branch and calls `window.showVortexRunningModal(() => {})` -- a HARDCODED EMPTY function as the retry callback. `showVortexRunningModal`'s own contract (shell.js) is to call whatever function it's given when the user clicks Try Again -- since this is always an empty no-op here, EVERY vortex-running error on this whole page (not just the scan-start case -- `rmfHandleError` is called from 11 different sites: initial load, vortex-data refresh, scan start, scan-stream errors, extract, download-archive, refresh-from-nexus, etc.) has a completely broken Try Again, always, regardless of what actually failed.

FIX: `rmfHandleError` needs to accept and forward a real retry function instead of hardcoding one. Add an optional third parameter (`retryFn`) to `rmfHandleError(e, box, retryFn)`, pass it through to `showVortexRunningModal(retryFn || (() => {}))` (falling back to a no-op only for call sites where there's genuinely nothing sensible to retry, e.g. a background stream error that isn't a discrete user action). Update EVERY call site (grep `rmfHandleError` -- there are 11) to pass the actual function that should re-run: the scan-start site should pass a function that re-calls the real scan-start logic, the extract site should retry the real extract call, etc. Don't fix only the scan-start case and leave the other 10 with the same silent-no-op bug -- this is a systemic issue in the shared helper, not a one-off.

VERIFY LIVE, the director's own exact repro at minimum: select collections, proceed to scan with Vortex still open, confirm the modal shows, close Vortex, click Try Again, confirm the scan ACTUALLY starts this time -- no need to go back to the picker. Also spot-check at least one other call site (e.g. Extract from Archive while Vortex happens to be open) to confirm Try Again works there too, not just the scan-start path. Handoff with what you tested and which call sites got a real retry vs. an intentional no-op (and why, for any left as no-op).
